Very interesting idea, but there are a few logical plot holes.

These noises include memetic kill-words such as “Cekliption”, “Diffechindic”, “Humplionicaned”, etcetera.

Why would you specifically spell out memetic kill agents in a document? Even if its a LVL5 one like you stated, that could count as something very volatile and dangerous.

I feel like you could really expand upon this concept - why does this SCP display the Berryman-Langford agent specifically if the agent is so volatile and used for one of the Foundation's most buried secrets? Why is it spreading it around? Is it trying to inoculate people against SCP-001's safety protocols? Is it trying to use them to kill people? I really hope that this gets a rewrite because I love the concept and it has so much potential.

item.title: Re: The Apocalypse Elevator
item.content:encoded:
Thank you, I am going to try again.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Normal elevator that when all the buttons are pushed it takes you to a world where humans are extinct.

Central Narrative:

  • Pushing all the buttons on this elevator causes the elevator and everything inside to get sent to a parallel universe.
  • In said universe; humans have been eradicated due to an unknown entity.
  • Any person who steps out of the elevator are met with an apocalyptic scene; a perpetual red haze in every direction, hollowed out husks of cars litter the streets, glass strewn across the road.
  • At first, every human they meet are long since dead, only skeletons remain.
  • The first living human they meet turns out to be from another alternate universe very similar to ours.
  • The other human leads them to a group of humans living in a bunker, hiding from the mysterious entity (SCP-XXXX-1).
  • These other humans are trying to fix the matching elevator from their alternate realities.
  • The human that just arrived has a degree in mechanics and fixes the elevator.
  • The humans step one after another into the elevator and pushes all the buttons and are sent back to their universe.
  • Just as the last 2 human are about to step into the elevator, SCP-XXXX-1 shows itself: a billowing swirl of red smoke, and "grabs" the closest human and the other human hears their screams as he is sent back to his universe.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Don't push all the buttons… or else…

item.title: Re: The Rube Effect
item.content:encoded:
Howdy hey! I'm KaraKatt and I'll be dropping a little bit of crit today!

+ Line by line and general thoughts.
- ...

Questions I Have While Reading Through

The virus is contagious but this is unknown by the Foundation at the time of the article's writing.

How do they find out that its a virus? They seem very blind to it.

The Subject was the child of two researchers who were killed in a containment breach. She's sent to live at the School for Children of Prominence. A short lived boarding school/orphanage program for children of Foundation personnel. She is notably idiotic and it amazes her teachers that she actually graduates.

I don't entirely see how this is important to the over arching story. Like, it gives back story, but I don't think you're going to have a way to slide it into the actual SCP.

After the article is submitted for review the higher ups begin to doubt the judgement of the lead researcher and try to have the SCP declassified due to 'lack or sufficient anomalous evidence'. The lead researcher is shunned and dives into a depressed drunken stupor.

Why would this lead to the Foundation shunning the researcher? If they just think its someone making things without evidence (or not enough) wouldn't they just shrug and give them a slap on the wrist?

Final notes

Hmm, this is interesting, but I don't think its quite there yet. You have a cool idea and a sort of story, but it feels like its missing some key parts to actually get its idea across. If the Foundation doesn't try to do stuff with the virus, then how would the reader ever know its a virus or even useable to the Foundation? I would also like to put in here that, because you're writing a human, you're going to need to characterize her. That's not saying to shove in backstory, but it is to say that you're going to need to show her idiocy.

Good luck!

item.title: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre:Mystery but mostly comedy

Page Layout:Scp article with story elements

Elevator Pitch

  • A blackmail envelope listing demands by the threat of release of information about the secret it is unknown what this secret is ,nor do they know if this envelop was meant for them.
  • This same envelop has been sent to other organizations with the exact same wording ,and It is not known who is sending this blackmail.
  • This blackmail seems appear ,and disappear at random intervals changing the demands between the period of absence via striking out the previous demands it also changes locations
  • It has the threat of revealing information about the secret to the public for now this secret is not known and of how severe this secret can be if revealed to the public.
  • It is unknown why this same message has been sent to other organizations, it is only known that this message has been sent to Wondertainment,Gamers Against Weed, Are We Cool Yet?, and previously mentioned SCP foundation. Currently under research if these organizations have anything in common.

central narrative:
The following message is enscribed in the blackmail at the moment of discovery :
"You Give all the yellow things bright things or we will tell everything about the secret so just make this eazy for both of us and just meet our demands ,sincerely you know who we are.

Contact information- 435-845-charity ,and the email(i thinkz this is like electrical email) charityEvent#moc.liamg|3#moc.liamg|3
Contact through the contact information has yielded in an automated voice call saying "thank you for Calling in our charity event please wait till one of our staff members can come thank you again for attending our charity event it is greatly appreciated.
The gmail is pending approval.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The mystery behind who is sending the blackmail , and the multiple details about for more in depth answers for the questions.

Additional Notes:The writing in the envelop has been written in poor English, The material used for writing the blackmail is mundane black ink, The blackmail disappearance and reappearance interval lasts 1 hour, and This appears in apparently random areas inside the foundation.

  • I would like some help with sending a picture I want to put in here to show the blackmail envelope.
  • Is there already a scp like this?
  • Is making the contact information having charity in it make it less enjoyable?
  • Would a interview with the gmail be interesting?
  • I would like some help with what i could replace the demands with.
  • I hope you all like this idea or maybe we can work together to make it into a better ideas all critique is appreciated.
  • I am sorry for the misleading summary i am just split on which idea would be better a charity or an unknown evil organization.

item.title: Re: Your Friendly Neighbourhood Thermonuclear Bomb
item.content:encoded:
This idea is absurd and I love it in every way possible. Okay, now I need to tell you why I'm not giving it a greenlight just yet.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

cooked via thermonuclear detonation

I want to know how it does this without killing everyone around it, nevermind just making the potato salad. Unless it was already pre-made and stored somewhere, I guess. Idk, but please expand on this and think about whether or not it would actually work. If you insist that it cooks potatoes by blowing them up (if you do insist on this, then I fucking love you) then please give specifics on how exactly that works. I don't mean atomically and chemically how, I mean how it does this without killing everyone in sight…….maybe the explosions don't affect people and it just affects potatos? :U idk. Something.

Also, the Central Narrative is just an extension of the Elevator Pitch; it continues to tell us what it's like, but not really giving any specific situations where it does this to people.

Think of some people, have them meet this thing and then do the song and dance of it telling them about the benefits of thermonuclear weaponry.

a disgruntled nuclear information evening worker dumped potato salad on the electronics causing it to move and speak.

If anything, maybe you could just expand this and use it as the plot. Doesn't need to be anything complicated; it's a cardboard cutout that loves thermonuclear weaponry and cooks potatoes with explosions.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day. 👍

item.title: Re: Immortal Fishception
item.content:encoded:
I think the Elevator Pitch is pretty damn hilarious considering this thing has another animal as its brain and I think this could have a bunch of potential, but sadly, the Central Narrative fails to go anywhere with it.

I've never used an SCP idea generator, but if something like this is par for the norm, then you really shouldn't rely on it. Get some inspiration, yes. Just take the idea from the generator and put it on the idea forums? No.

Give it a story. Why is there a goldfish in this thing's head? If you don't want to give an explanation as to why, then what effects does it have? Who's really in control here, the giant seahorse or the goldfish? Part of me imagines it's a goldfish that found a way to hijack the thing's brain and use its body as a way of gaining an advantage in the ecosystem. If you go the possession route, does it ever try to fight back against the mind control?

What shenanigans does it end up partaking in? Naturally, it will involve humans, since humans are curious creatures and a giant seahorse isn't exactly something normal.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day! 👍

There are a number of problems here, but the primary one is that this is merely a description.

SCPs are speculative fiction stories presented in the form of archival documents. Some are vignettes that paint an evocative scene over the course of a few paragraphs, some are sweeping multiple act novellas with twisting plots, some tell their stories through the ways that they toy with the framing itself… but at its core, every SCP is a story. That is the point of an SCP.

item.title: SCP Idea: "Albularyo"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: YES

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The basic SCP article layout.

Elevator Pitch:

  • Nato Caluag is an "albularyo", roughly translates to "witch doctor" in english who can conjure instances of "Engkantos" a Filipino mythological creature capable of applying a "sumpa" or curse.
  • This SCP is contained in a cell where he cannot have access to any object that could possibly have been marked with someone's DNA or even fingerprint. A microphone hidden from this SCP's sight must always be present inside his cell.
  • Moreover, any form of media that could potentially contain piece of a person's identity can never be shown to this SCP.
  • As long as this Albularyo sees a person of interest, obtain a piece of their DNA or even acquire an object with that person's fingerprint, if this SCP is in a hostile mood, he will have a "conversation" with an "Engkanto" who he claims to be his best friend and command it to lay a "sumpa" on the chosen victim. (This is why the microphone is necessary, because he verbally converses out loud.)
  • The random victim will experience immense pain on random parts of the body (chosen by Nato) and orifices of the victim will slowly discharge tadpoles and prematurely born insects.
  • Victims of this SCP can never die from the curse. However, the "sumpa" is able to be cured. Just not in a medical sense.
  • Scientific way of cure like medicine or surgery can NEVER prevent the "sumpa". BUT the only way to cure it is to take the victim to another "albularyo" who can perform the ritual of curse-removal.
  • To avoid this hostile activity, a full rosary and the "divine mercy" ritual must sincerely be recited every 3 in the afternoon. (Priests are usually called to perform the procedure and applied with memetics after)

Central Narrative:
Nato Caluag was considered a vengeful and hateful albularyo. Coincidentally, he was also a powerful one. Able to easily conjure Engkantos (who were actually the enemies of the witch doctors).
In the provinces of The Philippines, albularyos are considered healers and able to remove curses from victims. But Nato was the opposite of this and would apply the curse with the help of his "friend", an "Engkanto" that he met when he was young.
Nato grabbed the attention of the foundation after consecutive cases of unexplainable diseases were reported in the province of Bulacan.
Nato is actually the elder brother of Ed Caluag, a famous paranormal expert in Filipino mainstream media, but when the foundation took him, memetics were given to Ed and his family, completely forgetting his existence.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

  • Explores the pseudo-science belief of Filipino culture, especially the "albularyos" and "engkantos" with a unique take
  • This SCP can talk to engkantos and demand them to apply a curse ("sumpa") on a human, but this will never kill them, only make them suffer. And the only way to cure the curse is to find another albularyo capable of removing the curse.
  • Affiliation with a famous Filipino icon, but since he was taken by the foundation, his existence is not known to the public.

Additional Notes:

  • I'd gladly accept your critique on this and what should be improved.
  • I'd just like to know whether this idea is similar to an already-existing SCP or even tale?

I have the same problem with this that I do with a lot of "[religious, folk lore, or pop cultural thing] is back, in SCP format" articles. Namely, that much of the enjoyment and understanding that is derived from the specific ways in which the story is told and uses its medium. Stripped of the specific story-telling context, and not adapted to the medium of a SCP document, it loses almost all of its value as anything but a reference. Just as I wouldn't be interested in reading The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, The SCP Article, I wasn't particularly interested in reading this.

I will say that I enjoyed the dreamy quality of the recovered footage, but the article overall did little to nothing for me.

item.title: A joke SCP about amnestics(Seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A club classified as an SCP-J by the CKG Gathering due to its ability to erase memories if you swing it hard enough in the head.

Central Narrative: While on its search for methods to erase memories, the CKG Gathering discovers that hitting someone hard enough in the head with a club is able to erase memories. Therefore the club is classified as an anomalous "thing." The Foundation, of course, declares that the record is obsolete since they found a new method of erasing memories; hitting the head with an aluminium bat.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A photo of a club will be added for the readers to instantly notice what the "amnestic" is. Also, there will also be a parody of the amnestics guide page written in cavemen English. After this, I will add a modern revision of the object and will subvert the reader's expectation by revealing the Foundation simply decided to use other tools to bash heads, instead of using amnestics that we know.

Additional Notes: I want to know if there are other articles like this, or if it is better not to link it with SCP-001-EX-J.

This article has several handfuls of concepts that seem to have been pulled out of a hat - technicolor bats! cute names! mechanical geniuses! hats! not understanding basic concepts! That's not inherently a bad thing, but there's no narrative or even strong image/concept that can tie all these elements together.

The effect is like finding a heap of random clothes at Goodwill and being told that it's an outfit. -1
